ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Personalising a multi-view diffusion model on the input before lifting to 3D
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune a pretrained multi-view diffusion model on augmented crops and rotations of the single input image of the subject, using low-rank adapters, and add a few synthetic views produced by a personalised 2D model of the same subject. The adapted model then generates the full set of views that a native 3D reconstructor turns into an asset. We evaluate identity preservation on side and back views with an identity embedding model and human preference, on a benchmark of pets, toys and figurines with ground-truth multi-view captures.
CONTROLS: The unadapted multi-view model, score distillation with a personalised 2D prior, and a native 3D generator conditioned on the same image.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: Personalised multi-view generation should raise identity similarity on unseen views without hurting view consistency. Very thin structures may still be reconstructed poorly by the 3D stage.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Measuring identity preservation across viewpoints for generated 3D assets
PROPOSAL: We build an evaluation protocol for subject-driven 3D generation from captures of real subjects photographed from all sides. The generator receives one front view, and its renders at the held-out angles are compared with the real photographs using identity embeddings from several feature extractors, colour histogram distances and pairwise human judgements. We report scores by angle to show where identity is lost.
CONTROLS: Agreement between the automatic scores and the human judgements, scores of the real photographs against each other as an upper bound, and scores of a different subject of the same category as a lower bound.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Existing generators should lose identity mostly at back views, with colour shifts as a common failure. Feature extractors trained on faces may misjudge animal subjects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Correcting colour bias of multi-view diffusion with a subject-specific palette prior
PROPOSAL: We estimate a colour palette and texture statistics from the input image of the subject and add a guidance term during multi-view sampling that penalises deviations from these statistics in the generated views. This targets the systematic colour errors observed on unseen sides. We test on pets and objects whose back views share the front palette and on subjects whose back differs, to check that the prior does not erase real differences.
CONTROLS: Sampling without guidance, guidance with a palette from a different subject, and human ratings of colour faithfulness on held-out real views.
COST: 210
PREDICTION: Palette guidance should cut colour errors for uniform subjects. Subjects with distinct back patterns may be wrongly homogenised.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Personalised video-to-4D generation with a motion-aware identity adapter
PROPOSAL: We extend multi-view personalisation to dynamic subjects by fine-tuning a video multi-view diffusion model on frames of the input video, with an identity adapter shared across time and a motion module left frozen. The generated views at each time are then fused into a deformable 4D representation. We evaluate identity and motion fidelity on animal videos where a second camera captures the opposite side.
CONTROLS: The same pipeline without personalisation, per-frame image-to-3D personalisation without temporal sharing, and a score distillation 4D method.
COST: 760
PREDICTION: The shared identity adapter should keep appearance stable over time and preserve identity on the unseen side. Large non-rigid motion may reveal regions that no frame shows, limiting fidelity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Native 3D generation guided by personalised multi-view images
PROPOSAL: We combine the efficiency of a native 3D generator with the identity of a personalised multi-view model by feeding the generated personalised views as additional conditions to the native generator. We study how many views are needed and which angles matter most for identity, on a set of subjects with full real captures.
CONTROLS: The native generator with the single input image, the personalised views reconstructed by optimisation, and the native generator fed with unpersonalised views.
COST: 340
PREDICTION: Personalised views should raise identity on unseen sides while keeping the speed of native generation. Inconsistent views could introduce seams in the asset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Identity loss from averaging in score distillation
PROPOSAL: We quantify how score distillation averages appearance across samples of the diffusion prior by running it with priors of increasing personalisation strength on the same subject, and measure identity similarity and texture sharpness on rendered views. We then test a variant that anchors the distillation with views generated once by a personalised multi-view model.
CONTROLS: Standard score distillation, distillation with a personalised 2D prior, and the anchored variant, each with three random seeds.
COST: 420
PREDICTION: Stronger personalisation should improve identity but increase optimisation time, and anchoring should cut the averaging effect. Anchors with errors could be locked into the asset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A small multi-view dataset of personal subjects for evaluating 3D customisation
PROPOSAL: We collect turntable captures of household objects, toys and pets under controlled lighting, each with a casual front photo and a short handheld video, so that subject-driven 3D and 4D methods can be evaluated against real unseen views. We release masks, camera poses and identity annotations.
CONTROLS: Repeat captures of a subset to measure capture noise, inter-annotator agreement on identity annotations, and a check of pose accuracy against a calibration target.
COST: 30
PREDICTION: The dataset should reveal gaps between methods that synthetic benchmarks cannot show, especially for back views. Pets may be hard to capture consistently.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Synthesising identity-consistent training data for multi-view personalisation
PROPOSAL: Generate, with a personalised 2D diffusion model of the subject, a set of images from varied prompts describing other poses and viewpoints, filter them by identity similarity to the input, and use the survivors to fine-tune a multi-view model. This gives the multi-view model more than one image to learn the subject from. We test on subjects with asymmetric markings that reveal identity errors.
CONTROLS: Fine-tuning on the input image alone, fine-tuning on unfiltered synthetic images, and no fine-tuning.
COST: 380
PREDICTION: Filtered synthetic data should improve identity on unseen sides more than the input alone. If the 2D model invents wrong markings, filtering may not catch them.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Speed and quality trade-offs for subject-driven 3D generation
PROPOSAL: We measure the wall-clock time and the identity scores of personalised multi-view pipelines, score distillation pipelines and native 3D generators on the same subjects and hardware, to give practitioners a clear view of what each approach delivers per minute of generation. Results are broken down by subject category and viewing angle.
CONTROLS: Each pipeline without personalisation, the same subjects at two input resolutions, and repeated runs to estimate timing noise.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Personalised multi-view pipelines should offer the best identity per minute. Score distillation may match identity but take far longer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Composing several personalised subjects into one 3D scene
PROPOSAL: We generate separate personalised assets for two or three subjects from one image each and compose them into a scene, then check whether interactions such as occlusion or contact alter the identity of any subject in renders from new viewpoints. We also test a joint generation variant that personalises all subjects at once.
CONTROLS: Separate generation without personalisation, joint generation without personalisation, and identity scores of each subject rendered alone.
COST: 270
PREDICTION: Separate personalised assets composed afterwards should keep identity best. Joint personalisation may mix attributes between similar subjects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-view personalisation evaluated on real unseen views of each subject
PROPOSAL: We adapt a multi-view diffusion model to the single input image with low-rank adapters, generate views and reconstruct them into an asset, and test identity on side and back views against real photographs of the same subjects, which is the claim at stake.
CONTROLS: The unadapted multi-view model, score distillation with a personalised 2D prior, a native 3D generator, adaptation to a different subject of the same category as a placebo, identity embedding scores plus human ratings on the real held-out views, and results reported by viewing angle.
COST: 420
PREDICTION: Adaptation should raise identity on back views over all baselines while the placebo does not. If the placebo helps too, gains reflect category priors rather than identity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Low-rank adaptation of a multi-view diffusion model to one subject
PROPOSAL: We adapt a multi-view diffusion model to the single input image with low-rank adapters, generate views and reconstruct them into an asset, and score the results with a general image quality metric and a text-image similarity score against a caption of the subject.
CONTROLS: Two adapter ranks, two learning rates for the adapters, an ablation of image augmentation, results with two reconstruction back ends, a check that adaptation converges within a fixed step count, and a gallery of front renders for each subject.
COST: 420
PREDICTION: Quality and text similarity should stay high after adaptation. Higher ranks may overfit to the input pose.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Testing a colour palette prior against real back views
PROPOSAL: We add a guidance term to multi-view sampling that keeps generated views close to colour and texture statistics estimated from the input image, and test whether it fixes the colour errors on unseen sides without erasing real differences.
CONTROLS: Sampling without guidance, guidance with a palette from another subject as placebo, subjects whose back has distinct markings as a stress test, colour distances and human ratings against real held-out views, and separate results for uniform and patterned subjects.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Guidance should cut colour errors for uniform subjects. If patterned subjects lose their markings, the prior is too strong.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A colour palette guidance term for multi-view sampling
PROPOSAL: We add a guidance term to multi-view sampling that keeps generated views close to colour and texture statistics estimated from the input image, and present renders of the resulting assets with the average colour histogram distance between generated views.
CONTROLS: Two guidance weights, two colour spaces for the palette, an ablation of texture statistics, the term applied at early or late sampling steps, and timing of sampling with and without guidance.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Generated views should share a coherent palette. Stronger guidance may slightly reduce texture detail.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Personalised video-to-4D generation tested on the unseen side
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune a video multi-view diffusion model on the input video's frames with an identity adapter shared across time, fuse generated views into a deformable 4D asset, and check identity and motion on the side no frame shows, using a second camera as ground truth.
CONTROLS: The pipeline without personalisation, per-frame personalisation without temporal sharing, a score distillation 4D method, identity scores against the second camera per time step, motion error against tracked keypoints, and three seeds per subject.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: The shared adapter should keep identity stable over time on the unseen side. If per-frame personalisation matches it, temporal sharing brings nothing.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Personalised video-to-4D generation with a shared identity adapter
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune a video multi-view diffusion model on the input video's frames with an identity adapter shared across time, fuse generated views into a deformable 4D asset, and report temporal smoothness of the renders together with a frame quality score from a general aesthetic model.
CONTROLS: Two adapter placements in the network, two lengths of input clip, an ablation of the deformation regulariser, the asset rendered at two resolutions, and frame rate of rendering for each variant.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Renders should be smooth and pleasing over time. Longer input clips may improve smoothness slightly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: How many personalised views a native 3D generator needs for identity
PROPOSAL: We feed personalised multi-view images as extra conditions to a native 3D generator and vary the number and angles of these views, testing how identity on unseen sides changes against real captures of each subject.
CONTROLS: The native generator with the single input image, the same number of unpersonalised views as placebo, optimisation-based reconstruction from the personalised views, identity scores and human ratings on real held-out views, and results by viewing angle with three seeds.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: A few well-spread personalised views should give most of the identity gain. If unpersonalised views help equally, the gain is from view count rather than identity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Conditioning a native 3D generator on several generated views
PROPOSAL: We feed personalised multi-view images as extra conditions to a native 3D generator and vary the number and angles of these views, reporting the mesh quality and the generation time for each configuration on a set of household subjects.
CONTROLS: Two view resolutions, two encoders for the extra conditions, an ablation of view ordering, mesh face counts per configuration, and the generator run with mixed and full precision.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: More views should give cleaner meshes at slightly higher generation time, with diminishing returns once the main angles are covered. View ordering and the choice of encoder may matter little for the final mesh.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does anchoring score distillation on personalised views stop identity averaging
PROPOSAL: We test whether score distillation loses identity through averaging by running it with priors of increasing personalisation on the same subject, and whether anchoring on personalised multi-view images removes the loss, measuring identity on real unseen views.
CONTROLS: Standard distillation, distillation with a personalised 2D prior, the anchored variant, anchors from a different subject as placebo, identity scores and texture sharpness against real held-out views, and three seeds per setting.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Anchoring should cut averaging and raise identity on unseen sides. Wrong anchors would lock their errors into the asset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anchoring score distillation with personalised multi-view images
PROPOSAL: We run score distillation with priors of increasing personalisation on the same subject, anchor the optimisation on personalised multi-view images, and report how quickly the optimisation converges together with sharpness of the rendered textures.
CONTROLS: Two anchor loss weights, two schedules for the guidance scale, an ablation of the anchor resolution, optimisation time to a fixed loss value, and the number of iterations per configuration.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Anchored distillation should converge faster with sharper textures. High anchor weights may slow early iterations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Subject-adapted multi-view generation for identity in unseen views
PROPOSAL: We adapt a multi-view diffusion model to the subject from its single image, enriched with synthetic views from a personalised 2D model filtered by identity similarity, and lift the generated views to 3D with a native reconstructor, so that every viewpoint is generated with knowledge of this specific subject.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model, score distillation with a personalised prior, a native 3D generator, and identity scores on real unseen views.
COST: 460
PREDICTION: Identity on back views should improve clearly. Thin structures may still fail in reconstruction.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Higher-resolution multi-view generation for detailed 3D assets
PROPOSAL: We upscale the views produced by a multi-view diffusion model with a super-resolution diffusion stage and lift them to 3D with a native reconstructor, so that every viewpoint of the asset carries finer texture detail than the base model gives. The single input image of the subject conditions the base model as before.
CONTROLS: The base model at native resolution, score distillation with a personalised prior, a native 3D generator, and identity scores on real unseen views.
COST: 460
PREDICTION: Texture detail should improve clearly on all views. Upscaling may sharpen colour errors on the back.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Correcting systematic colour errors on unseen sides of a subject
PROPOSAL: We estimate the subject's palette and texture statistics from the input and guide multi-view sampling to respect them, targeting the colour shifts that generators show on views not covered by the input, and we check on subjects with distinct backs that real differences survive.
CONTROLS: Unguided sampling, a palette from another subject, colour distances against real held-out views, and human ratings.
COST: 190
PREDICTION: Colour errors should fall for uniform subjects. Distinct markings on the back must survive the guidance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Filtering the training data of multi-view diffusion models
PROPOSAL: We filter the large object datasets used to train multi-view diffusion models, removing renders with unusual lighting or tinted materials by a learned quality classifier, and retrain the model on the filtered set, on the view that cleaner data reduce colour shifts in generated views of any object.
CONTROLS: The model trained on unfiltered data, random filtering of equal size, colour distances against real held-out views, and human ratings.
COST: 190
PREDICTION: Colour shifts should fall for common objects. The approach needs a full retraining of the base model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Identity-preserving 4D assets from a single video of the subject
PROPOSAL: We personalise a video multi-view diffusion model on the input video with an identity adapter shared across time and fuse its outputs into a deformable 4D representation, so that sides of the subject that the video never shows are generated with its own appearance and stay consistent as it moves.
CONTROLS: Unpersonalised generation, per-frame personalisation, a score distillation 4D method, and identity scores against a second camera.
COST: 680
PREDICTION: Identity on the unseen side should hold over time. Large motions may expose regions without cues.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Realistic motion transfer for 4D assets from a single video
PROPOSAL: We extract a skeleton and motion trajectory from the input video and retarget it onto a 3D asset generated from the first frame, so that the asset moves like the subject in the video, with a physics-based correction step that removes foot sliding and interpenetration during the motion.
CONTROLS: Unpersonalised generation, motion copied without correction, a score distillation 4D method, and motion error against a second camera.
COST: 680
PREDICTION: Motion should match the video closely. The asset's appearance stays that of the first-frame generation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Benchmark of identity preservation on real multi-view captures
PROPOSAL: We capture real subjects from all sides, give each generator a single front view, and score renders at held-out angles against the real photographs with identity embeddings and human judgements, so that the field can measure the faithfulness of side and back views directly.
CONTROLS: Real photographs against each other as ceiling, a different subject of the same category as floor, and agreement between automatic scores and humans.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Back views should show the largest identity losses. Face-trained embeddings may misjudge animals.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Benchmark of geometric accuracy for single-image 3D generation
PROPOSAL: We scan real subjects with a structured-light scanner, give each generator a single front view, and score the generated meshes against the scans with chamfer distance and normal consistency, so that the field can measure the shape accuracy of side and back regions directly.
CONTROLS: Repeated scans of the same subject as ceiling, a different subject of the same category as floor, and agreement between metrics and humans.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Back regions should show the largest shape errors. Thin parts may be missed by every method.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Personalised views as conditions for fast native 3D generation
PROPOSAL: We generate a small set of views of the subject with a multi-view model personalised on its input image and pass them to a native 3D generator as extra conditions, combining the identity of personalisation with the speed of generation without per-scene optimisation, and we score identity on real unseen views.
CONTROLS: The native generator with one image, unpersonalised views, optimisation-based reconstruction, and three seeds.
COST: 330
PREDICTION: Identity should improve while generation stays fast. View inconsistency may cause seams.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling a native 3D generator into a smaller model
PROPOSAL: We distil a large native 3D generator into a smaller student that conditions on the single input image and produces an asset in one forward pass, combining the quality of the large generator with lower memory and faster generation for real-world use, and we score identity on real unseen views.
CONTROLS: The large generator with one image, a student trained from scratch, optimisation-based reconstruction, and three seeds.
COST: 330
PREDICTION: The student should keep most of the quality at a fraction of the memory. Fine details may be lost.
